stories.title: 436,000 Sole Traders and Landlords Make Their Tax Digital
stories.summary: HMRC reports that 436,000 sole traders and landlords have signed up for Making Tax Digital for Income Tax. From September, HMRC will begin signing up remaining customers required to use MTD for the 2026-27 tax year.

stories.title: 13 Asylum Hotels Exited and Returned to Local Communities
stories.summary: The Home Office has exited 13 asylum hotels, returning them to local communities. The department has also begun discussions to explore the use of 3 new former MoD sites to house asylum seekers.

stories.title: Ministers Push Ahead with Housing Asylum Seekers on Ex-Military Bases
stories.summary: Home Office minister Anna Turley has confirmed the government is sticking with plans to accommodate asylum seekers on former military bases, despite ongoing protests from local residents.

stories.title: Gig Goers Urged to Stop! Think Fraud Before Buying Tickets
stories.summary: The Home Office is running a campaign urging music event attendees to be vigilant about fraud when purchasing concert and festival tickets online.

stories.title: Joint Statement on Executions in Iran
stories.summary: The UK's Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office issued a joint international statement condemning executions in Iran, calling on the Iranian government to end the use of the death penalty.

stories.title: Foreign Secretary Miliband Announces First Major Russia Sanctions Package
stories.summary: Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband has unveiled the UK's first major Russia sanctions package under his tenure, reaffirming the UK's unwavering support for Ukraine.

stories.title: Syria Social Cohesion Programme: Integrated Security Fund
stories.summary: The FCDO's UK Office for Syria has invited Syrian civil society organisations to submit proposals for a new social cohesion programme, with a deadline of 11 September.

stories.title: Timms Review: Workshops Open to Shape PIP Recommendations
stories.summary: The DWP's Timms Review steering group is inviting disabled people and those with long-term health conditions across the UK to register interest in shaping workshops for its Personal Independence Payment review recommendations.

stories.title: Just 20 of 6,600 Defra Staff Working on Climate Adaptation Amid Drought and Wildfires
stories.summary: An investigation has revealed that only 20 out of Defra's 6,600 staff are working on climate adaptation, raising serious concerns about the UK's preparedness as the country faces ongoing drought and wildfire crises during the 2026 heatwave.

stories.title: UK Heatwave: Burnham Considers Ban on Disposable Barbecues to Prevent Wildfires
stories.summary: Manchester Mayor Andy Burnham is considering banning disposable barbecues as UK wildfires continue to rage during the current extreme heat event, with the government's COBRA emergency committee involved in the response.

stories.title: UK and Australia Boost Radar Technology and Industry Cooperation
stories.summary: A new agreement will see UK and Australian defence firms collaborate on cutting-edge radar systems, as the UK Defence Minister visits Indo-Pacific partners to strengthen bilateral defence ties and boost growth across both nations' defence industries.

stories.title: Country Policy Note Updated: Russian Military Service (August 2026)
stories.summary: The MoD has updated its country policy and information note on Russian military service, clarifying the status of Russian reservists and the implications of the September 2022 partial mobilisation decree for asylum and immigration cases.

stories.title: DBT Renamed as Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade (BIST)
stories.summary: Following machinery of government changes announced on 20 July 2026, the Department for Business and Trade (DBT) has been renamed the Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade (BIST), taking on additional science and technology responsibilities.

stories.title: Government Responds to CMA Review of UK Subsidy Control Act
stories.summary: The UK government has published its response to the Competition and Markets Authority's review of the Subsidy Control Act's effectiveness, addressing its impact on competition and investment across the UK.

stories.title: Precarious Work and Economically Inactive Survey Published
stories.summary: DBT has published a new technical report examining the impacts of working in precarious employment, drawing on survey data from people in low-income and economically inactive situations across the UK.

agencies.name: DSIT
agencies.description: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology

stories.title: DSIT Functions Absorbed into New Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade
stories.summary: As part of the July 2026 machinery of government changes, DSIT's science and technology functions have been absorbed into the newly formed Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade (BIST), marking a significant restructuring of the UK's science and innovation policy landscape.

stories.title: Over a Quarter of NHS Staff Lose More Than 10 Hours a Week to Admin
stories.summary: A new survey from NHS Shared Business Services has found that more than 25% of NHS staff spend over 10 hours per week on administrative tasks, highlighting a significant productivity drain that AI and automation tools could help address.

stories.title: NHS Devon Publishes Digital Inclusion Delivery Plan
stories.summary: NHS Devon Integrated Care Board has published a Digital Inclusion Delivery Plan, setting out how the organisation will ensure all residents can access NHS digital services, amid ongoing concerns about medical staffing levels.

stories.title: King's College Hospital Moves to Digital Letters and Appointments
stories.summary: King's College Hospital NHS Foundation Trust is transitioning outpatient appointment information and clinic letters to digital delivery via email and text message, reducing paper and improving patient communication.

stories.title: Royal Mail Apologises for 'Unacceptable' Service
stories.summary: Royal Mail has issued an apology for what it described as an 'unacceptable' level of service in some areas of the UK, following customer complaints about delayed deliveries and missed collections.
